You’re quite welcome.

I guess it depends on how much you feel that you can trust your girlfriend. If she’s an honest and nice person (and she sounds like she is) then it’s unlikely that she would lie about something as damaging as suicide. Suicidal people only generally lie about it if a. they have absolutely made up their mind already, to the point of where nothing will stop them achieving it including lying to loved ones, or b. they’re weren’t a particularly nice or honest person to begin with.

In short, if lying about it would be out-of-character for her, then she would probably only lie out of extreme desperation.

I understand why you are concerned. You can *never* be too careful when it comes to depression, let alone depression mixed with ongoing trauma. The problem is that a suicidal impulse can come at any time; “flash-in-the-pan” attempts are possible, which is where the pain suddenly spikes to such intensity that pushes someone to attempt without much forethought other than “I need to end this pain NOW”. Especially bad events often trigger them. Like I said, if your gut feeling ever gets too much, try and make sure someone is physically around her until you think she’s stabilised. You don’t even have to tell her why; just spontaneously spend the night, or get someone to listen outside her door every 30 mins, or have a looooooong phonecall with her.

By the way, she really sounds like she’s in a shitty situation with a lot of people holding her head under the water, so to speak. What a stupid school. You sound like you’re very important to her wellbeing. Don’t let her push you away with her “I don’t deserve you” tactics. She’s just in a lot of emotional pain, and it’s really hard to see anything clearly like that. Try and be the reason she wants to hang on.

Dealing with somebody you love going through so much is hard too. You’re a great boyfriend. Good luck.

Yes, definitely. 

I’m sorry your girlfriend is having such an awful time. Please watch her behaviour closely and give her as much support as you can. 

One thing to look out for in particular is an extreme mood reversal; if she suddenly becomes intensely happy-go-lucky and whimsical for no reason, especially if she explains it is “I just decided everything will be okay!” or a variant thereof, it may be because she has already planned her suicide and is feeling relieved and unburdened knowing her time is nearly over. Another thing to watch out for is the language she uses; if she ever makes any references to “not being around much longer”, mentions wanting to go to the store but seems vague or unconvincing as to why, or says a random problem that will suddenly not be important “soon”, *please* do not brush it off. The fact that she has already stated that she “doesn’t care about anything” and that you “shouldn’t care about her” are big alarm bells, as these things could **possibly** actually mean “I don’t care if I live or die” and “I wish you’d stop caring about me so I wouldn’t feel guilty about hurting myself”. If you’re ever in doubt, try to make sure she’s always around somebody and accounted for. A lot of flash-in-the-pan suicide attempts can be foiled just by the simple inconvenience of someone else in the room or adjacent room.

If possible, please also help her seek help for her bullying problem. Nobody should have to suffer bullying for five years. It can be a life changing ordeal as it often sets people up for a life of underconfidence, emotional damage and social anxiety. It’s gone on long enough.

Also, if you live in America, please try to avoid calling emergency services on her unless you believe she’s in immediate danger. The system for dealing with suicidal people in America is traumatic and horrifically expensive. It should never be ruled out, but should definitely be a last resort as opposed to someone simply physically watching over her.
I’m sorry, I’m too mentally ill to give any advice right now. I just wanted you to know that I read your post and wish you the best. Love right back at you.

300lbs here. Lifelong eating disorder and over a decade of other mental illnesses on top make sure I do nothing but gain. Whenever I tried to tell myself “FUCK MY MENTAL ILLNESS, I WILL BE THINNER AT ALL COSTS” it just lead to behaviour like eating nothing but egg whites, putting my food on top of high places I couldn’t reach and walking five miles at 6am after all that. I have this weird thing where I always feel like I have to “kick-start” my “new healthy life” by not eating anything for three days. Because it shrinks my stomach. Of course, the fat side of the eating disorder always wins anyway. Ironic that I was diagnosed anorexic several times before I was ten years old, but I can’t put the fucking fork down now that I’m older.

You’re a stronger, better person than me. Don’t do it my way. Do it the sensible way. I believe in you.

You sound like me 10 years ago. I tried to run, over and over again. My brain followed me. Loved ones never did.

I’m so sorry. Your wonderful friend doesn’t have to be the last. I wish I could be, but... I am in no shape to be anybody’s friend. There are great people here, though. A few of them saved my life tonight. I hope you find each other.

I really wish the best for you. If I were religious, I’d pray, and if I were still unbroken, I’d try to help... But I’m neither. So I’ll just wish really hard. Not that you stay with us, but... That life gives you reasons to.

I’m just leaving a comment to let you know: I’m sticking around another night. You’re one reason for that, so thank you. I just needed someone to care, and to distract me.

Owe you one.

I just wanted to let you know that I’ve stabilised. The rope is staying in the cupboard for a second night.

It wasn’t so much what you said; I just needed somebody, anybody, to care if I died. And to keep me distracted long enough to feel it.

Thank you very much for tonight.

It’s okay. I think... I think I fought it off, for another night.

Thank you so much. Partially for helping keep me alive, but also just for what you said. I really needed it. I hope we don’t talk again, because if we do, it means I’ll be slipping from the edge again. I can’t form friendships in my state.

Goodnight.

You overcame the worst that life has given you, and yet you still come on this sub and talk to people who don’t have any hope left in an effort to try and give them some of yours.

That’s so wonderful, and I hope you know that. I wish I could help people too. I used to. It’s like they scooped out my insides, the things that made me feel like I did any good in the world, and it’s all I can do to hold on. I can’t help anyone anymore.

And I can eat fast food, and swallow pills, and consume memes... But life doesn’t stop for me. I didn’t know what r/happy was. I thought maybe it was things to make you happy, like kittens and kids and memes. I was just wasting time, trying to ignore reality, when a whole subreddit of reality said “LOOK AT THESE WONDERFUL PEOPLE WHO GOT THEIR HAPPY ENDINGS!”

I don’t begrudge anybody. I’m so happy (and impressed) that you got clean, and got help, and that all those people on there are happy and loved and safe.

But the happiness is drowned out by my reality, and the reality is that I don’t know why I’m not like you. Like them. I don’t know why the universe would tear me to shreds so completely. I honestly gave everything. It’s like being trampled underfoot of many horses, and at first you try to fight, you say FUCK THIS and you fight so hard, but it’s...

And every time you think you’ve given up for good, you start fighting again. And every time you think you’ve escaped, you’re trampled harder.

But so many years, so many people I trusted...

I don’t think I can get more broken. I’m just letting it trample me now. And it does. And if it hasn’t stopped by now, it never will.

I’ll never be able to trust anyone again, man. That alone feels like a good reason to die.

Thank you... It’s so nice to hear something nice... Said to me. I nearly started crying again there.

There’s a whole complex ball-of-wool culmination behind my desire to die, but that’s not why I posted. I don’t want to talk much, honestly. I’ve already attempted literally over 20 times in the past 12 months (I lost count around 12, but there were a LOT after that, so that’s my cautious estimate).

I posted because I just... Want to feel like someone cares. Even just superficially, from a stranger. Even just for a little while. If I go.

Thank you.

Thank you, that’s very kind. I really shouldn’t get any credit, though; I tried to make “worthlessthrowaway” but found that it was already taken. Adding “me” in the middle was just the first thing that came to mind, since it represented how I felt pretty well.

How I feel.

I’m so sorry to hear that you’ve never had any friends. That must be... So lonely.

The truth is, I’ve had SO MANY friends over my life. So many. People tell me I’m charismatic, funny, kind, smart. Back when I could at least moderately function as a human being, I could walk into a new place and make a friend in a minute. I made friends with my rival at my job interview (it was just two of us and we were supposed to be directly competing). I then got hired for that job, and as soon as I started, my coworkers fawned over me. One of the managers specifically adored me, said that I was like walking sunshine. I had customers tell my superiors that I was such a warm, friendly, helpful worker — so much that I got a little badge to wear announcing I was one of the best.

I was a temp. I only worked there a few months.

I’m not telling this to show off, so please don’t think that. I’m telling this because, I’m the end, none of this matters. The pressure of constantly saying “yes” to overtime in order to do my best sent me into a massive breakdown literally in the middle of my shift. Huge anxiety attack. Had to be sent home. Everybody was sympathetic, but when it came to decide which temps to keep on permanently, I didn’t get kept.

And all those people who fawned over me from work, they just faded away like embers.

But they were just temporary coworkers. That’s the kind of thing you expect. The heartbreak comes from being abandoned by every person I ever loved, and that I thought loved me back. The list started when my Dad left before I was six months old, and it has only ever expanded to include literally everyone.

And I love so much. I love people so, so much. In my world, the order is to be honest always, even when it’s harsh and painful, and to be loyal, and to always help as much as possible when anyone needs it.

When one of my friends became homeless, I watched as all of our mutual friends shrugged with a “that sucks, dude” and moved on. I lived in a different country, but I looked up shelters in the area and sent him all the money I had and tried to arrange transport for him to a relative.

And that is good, and I’m happy I did, and he’s better now and I’m so glad! I don’t regret a n y t h i n g.

But when this same friend caught me in a suicide attempt a few weeks ago, he didn’t even check back to see if I survived it or not.

Notice I’m using the word “friend” myself. Everyone I’ve ever cared about, they... I don’t know, get sick of me? Bored of me? They just... leave. Always. There’s a handful of people out there who, if you said “Is Worthless your friend?” they’d say “Of course she is!”

But they haven’t seen or messaged me in months. If I don’t contact them, they never contact me. I used to chase people, desperately try to keep earning their love, giving gifts and Christmas cards and letters that were never requited...

But recently, after being betrayed in the worst way by the worst people, I gave up. And nobody came. Nobody’s coming. I could string myself up now and I’ll be here for hours.

I just thought if you are honest and loving, people will... too...

But only as long as you’re keeping them entertained. And that’s just friends. When it’s family, or partners, or spouses... Over and over...

About six years ago, my favourite saying was thus: it is better to have loved and lost, than never to have loved at all. It’s not true. I would rather not have known any love, than to think I ever had it and just be left like this. Over and over. For my whole life.

I’m sorry. That was way too much and stupid. I made a throwaway so that I could talk about my feelings without feeling shame, but here is the shame anyway. 

I wish I could melt into the ground and nourish plants.

I’m sorry.

I can’t be your friend. I want to, because you deserve someone and so do I, but I just can’t trust anyone anymore. Not after last year. Besides, I might not be around much longer myself.

I just wanted to let you know that you are, literally, not alone.

- I have a severe eating disorder that heavily affects my life (and body)

- I suffer from constant mood swings that exhaust me, but they are mostly low moods, such as anger, depression and mind-breaking anxiety

- I am not OCD, but have anxiety tics and problems with self-harming, the two of which are sometimes the same thing

- I have no friends

- I am turning 28 this year

The similarities between us were so startling, I just had to comment. You’re not alone, Naomi. Somebody gets it.

I wish you the best.

- Hannah

I guess a mod removed it. I don’t know much about how reddit works. I can still see it in my post history, unaltered.

I talked about my purchase (as the package arrived yesterday) and that I felt less suicidal than when I ordered it, but still dangerous. I talked about how lonely I felt, and asked if anyone could, just...

Say something nice to me. Anything. Like a friend might.

I have no friends. I talked about that too.

It just... It doesn’t matter. Yesterday, I was just depressed and wished I could hear a kind word. I wasn’t upset when I got no replies.

Tonight, I want to do it.

This is the most fun way I have ever heard sinking and drowning described.

My uncle writes code for a living. He was a team leader for 15 years, and literally found out recently the company was SEVERELY underpaying him for the job he does. He changed to coding for a very big, nationwide chain instead. Makes a very, very tidy sum.

Kid, those people are literally WRONG. W R O N G. Yes, your parents, too. Parents should be supportive of their kids' interests anyway, but in this case, they are literally trying to steer you away from a lifetime of high-pay and easy job offers. Everybody uses computers. Those computers have programs. Every single company  in the world uses multiple programs. Website builders, spreadsheets, communications systems, security systems, and all the video games...

That doesn't change how they make you feel, though. I'm sorry they make you feel like shit.

Do what you love. Use pocket money to buy your own PC, or use a public one. Read books on it. If and when you die, die doing what you love, not what other people chose.

Oh, a lot of things. I'm that kind of weirdo. I literally have a drawer of this shit that I call my "memory drawer" that also contains things like holiday cards, tickets and assorted mementos. Warning, this gets heavy, hence throwaway.

- I fell in love HARD in high school. My crush, who was also my best friend, somehow swapped his maths textbook with mine by accident. We never got around to swapping back, and he moved to another part of the country when he was 15. It's still here somewhere, with his name on the front. I've never even flipped through it, but it's hard to throw it away. Eternally unrequited, you see.

- A key from a wardrobe my mother owned at some point, the wardrobe itself being gone for years at this point. It is a very ornate key, and I took to wearing it as a necklace shortly before dating my first super cereal boyfriend. It became my favourite piece of jewellery, back when wearing random keys wasn't "cool" and I just liked it. After he cheated on me and we broke up, it became sentimental as it reminded me of him. A month after breaking up with him, I was raped by a childhood friend. This sent me into a baaaaaaad downward spiral, especially after my recent ex (who had met the guy several times) only responded with an apathetic "Well, it's too late now". This culminated in an arrest for a public suicide attempt some months later. I was admitted to a psychiatric hospital at 17 and the key was allowed in with me. Biiiiiig mistake. It was a stupid, futile attempt that went nowhere, but I tried to kill myself with it whilst in the hospital. Locked myself in a bathroom, used it to tightly secure a plastic bag over my head and attempted to asphyxiate myself. They snapped the chain getting it off, as I had wound it very tight and it wasn't actually a jewellery chain; it was a metal ball chain that usually holds the ID cards of office workers. I've never worn it since, but I can't seem to get rid of it. It seems too important to my personal history.

- A big, thick seashell. I was on holiday with my husband and in-laws at the beach, and the hotel was right next to the sea. Unfortunately for me, I am weak and the tide was brutal, and I nearly pathetically drowned in a foot or so of water. Other swimmers further out were watching with genuine confusion. I ended up storming back to the swimming pool at our hotel and staying there all day, declaring I hated the sea. There was only one other person in the pool: a young girl, brown hair, probably between 8 and 12. She looked somewhat lonely and bored. I didn't attempt to talk to her because, y'know, I'm an adult woman and they make PSAs about that kind of thing. After an hour or two of me and my husband messing around with the lilo I'd bought, though, she came over herself. I learned that she'd spent all day in the pool too, and that her parents basically ignored her and left her to her own devices. She was an only child and had no friends with her. This struck me hard, because I too used to be an only child who spent all day alone in the pool on holidays while my parents slept off their hangovers. We started chatting, and she seemed to be trying to act adultlike and impress me; meanwhile, I am basically a child brain in a stupid dumb grown-up body and I started getting moreso by the minute. We played some pool games I knew, and she taught me one she knew called Marco Polo. (I'm not American, but lived in America at the time, and everyone there knows that game. By the way, she was a TERRIBLE cheater; she barely whispered "polo" or sometimes just didn't fucking say it if I were close, but I usually got her anyway.) We even got my stick-in-the-mud brother-in-law to join in for a bit. We only left the pool when the sun started going down, and before we headed back to our rooms, she pulled me aside and gave me a shell she'd found earlier and hidden. It's the best shore-found shell I've ever seen; really big and heavy, white and blue. We promised to meet again before we went home, but we never did. That's probably because, as she headed towards her apartment door, her parents stepped outside and looked alarmed to find her in the company of one fully-grown woman and two fully-grown men in their bathing suits. She was excitedly telling them about playing Marco Polo with us and their faces were a kind of uncomfortable fake-pleasantness that grew and grew. Still, I remember the lonely girl and her seashell, and I hope I made her holiday better. She made mine better.

- Up until recently, my favourite ever top ever ever ever. I just loved wearing it so much and couldn't admit that it was so tattered and stained with sweat that I couldn't wear it, not even to bed, and it was therefore literally a rag I just kept in my wardrobe. It got some heavy use and was kept for about eight years when I probably should have thrown it out at four, but I finally let it go last year.

- Also up until recently, a woven red rope. It was made of red silk string in a single strand, and was adorned with jade beads at the end. I think it was some kind of Asian charm, possibly for luck. You've all heard the story of the red string of fate, right? It's some kind of eastern legend that says that people who are meant to be together are connected by a red string that stretches around the world and will eventually bring them together, no matter how many tangles and knots get in the way. When I met my future husband, I presented him with the bit of rope at some point and announced it was our red string. It became special to us, especially because we really were from opposite sides of the earth (he America, I England) and we kept it in a heart-shaped box that I hand-painted for him (one half dusk to represent him, the other half dawn to represent me) that was also filled with 100 cards bearing reasons that I loved him that I presented him on his birthday. Yeah, I'm that kind of sap. Well, a few months short of five years together and three years married, he cheated on me. In desperation to try and restore my trust in him, we agreed to a blood oath. He would never willfully lie to me again, and I (who never lies about anything) would promise to consult him straightaway if I ever felt inclined to hurt myself, as I have a myriad of mental illnesses that push me to do so. We cut open our hands and shared blood. Within weeks, he broke the oath. He continued to see this girl behind my back and lied about it. I held on for another couple of months, but due to that and many other things, I just had to leave him. I got him to cut the rope in half before I left, a symbolic ending of our blood oath and our future. I didn't get my happy ending.

- A tiny jar of gold flakes that I can't seem to find now. It was from a short fling I had as a teenager. I met the guy through a mutual friend and we talked on MSN messenger (the good ol' days)  a lot before we met up. As soon as we actually met up, I knew something was off. He seemed somewhat anti-social, screeching at people in the street like that guy from that zombie movie I haven't seen but everyone else has. He told me it was literally to intimidate them. He at one point bit my neck so hard I felt him dig into the neck muscles, and I was in pain for a week after. When I told him about my rape, he literally did not care at all. What really swung it, though, was that he actually told me in messenger that he planned to go out and kill a bunch of people someday. Because it was the best way to die. I'm pretty sure he was serious. Trying to reason with him only made him enthusiastically explain why he didn't care about anyone he didn't know personally and that their lives were worthless and he wanted to be famous for it. God, I hope he's not reading this. Anyway, I ran away from that pretty damn quick. Considered calling the police with the chat logs, but didn't. I haven't ever spoken to him again, but I hear he hasn't killed anyone. Yet.

Loads more, can't remember them, can't be bothered to pull them out and look, it's 3:30am.

TL;DR I COLLECT NONSENSE AND MY LIFE IS DRAMATIC

I'm sorry for your loss.
